comparison: Both evaluate protein-protein interaction claims (C3, C47-C54). OpenEval finds the MS/MS immunoprecipitation data with biological quadruplets and validation of three interactors supportive. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, noting interactions are 'tentative' and may not be direct since pulldown mixed E. coli and Msm lysates, requiring additional validation.

Both address the integrative model linking tethering to lipid homeostasis (C12, C90-C91). OpenEval finds the model well-supported by totality of evidence as a coherent framework. Peer reviewers express uncertainty, stating the causal link 'requires additional proof' and is interpretive rather than directly demonstrated.

Both address background/literature claims (C1-C2, C13-C32, C101-C103). OpenEval finds these well-supported as established knowledge appropriately cited. Peer reviewers accept this background context without challenge, acknowledging it as foundation for 'an important study.'

Both evaluate NAO staining and CL localization claims (C73-C75, C93, C95). OpenEval finds NAO data supportive of CL mislocalization with rigorous quantification. Peer reviewers express uncertainty about interpretation, suggesting distinction between 'lipid homeostasis' versus 'lipid localization' effects requires clarification.

Both evaluate morphological changes from Wag31 depletion (C33-C38, C92). OpenEval finds SEM/TEM imaging with quantification and CFU data well-supportive. Peer reviewers agree the data are 'solid and support the conclusion made,' accepting morphological phenotypes.

Both evaluate lipidomics data showing lipid dysregulation (C4-C5, C42-C46). OpenEval finds LC-MS data with six biological replicates well-supportive. Peer reviewers agree, stating 'data presented are solid' and 'importance of Wag31 in maintaining lipid homeostasis is supported,' with minor clarifications requested.

Both evaluate domain dissection experiments (C8, C84-C89, C99). OpenEval finds His-pulldown experiments with deletion mutants supportive of domain-specific functions. Peer reviewers strongly agree, with multiple reviewers affirming the 'detailed analysis of Wag31 domain architecture revealed distinct functional roles.'

Both evaluate CL binding specificity claims (C6, C55-C56, C94, C120). OpenEval finds PLiMAP assays with defined liposomes well-supportive of preferential CL binding. Peer reviewers agree, stating 'clear link to interactions with CL is shown' and findings are 'convincingly demonstrated.'

Both evaluate membrane tethering assays (C63-C67, C117-C119). OpenEval finds fluorescent liposome clustering experiments with quantification supportive. Peer reviewers agree, affirming the 'interaction between Wag31 and cardiolipin' and tethering activity are 'convincingly demonstrated.'

Both evaluate complementation experiments with mutants (C78-C83). OpenEval finds BODIPY and NAO staining of complementation strains supportive of tethering's functional importance. Peer reviewers agree, noting 'studies using mutant versions of Wag31 shed light on the functionalities of each domain.'

Both evaluate PLiMAP assays with Wag31 mutants (C7, C57-C62, C68-C69, C98, C100, C112-C116). OpenEval finds differential effects of K20A versus ΔN mutations supportive of separable functions. Peer reviewers agree on the N-terminal role, affirming 'role of the N-terminus in this interaction was convincingly demonstrated.'

Both evaluate essentiality of N-terminal domain (C9-C11, C76-C77). OpenEval finds complementation experiments with multiple assays supportive that Wag31ΔN cannot rescue depletion. Peer reviewers agree on domain importance but note (in R6) that causal mechanism linking tethering to survival requires additional proof.

Both address ILI formation and lipid accumulation (C39-C41, C104-C105). OpenEval finds BODIPY staining with quantification supportive. Peer reviewers accept lipid dysregulation findings broadly, with R2 noting 'clear that both depletion and overexpression have an effect on levels of various lipids.'

Partial overlap on mechanistic interpretations (C110-C111). OpenEval acknowledges these are speculative hypotheses reasonably inferred from data. Peer reviewers similarly note the mechanistic link between tethering and lipid homeostasis 'requires additional proof.'

Minimal overlap on background claims about CL microdomains (C70-C72, C96-C97). OpenEval finds these appropriately cited as established knowledge. Peer reviewers accept background context without challenge.

Minimal overlap on comparison to B. subtilis DivIVA (C112-C116). OpenEval notes speculation about functional differences is reasonable but not experimentally tested. Peer reviewers do not specifically comment on these comparative claims.

Minimal overlap on interactor localization analysis (C106-C109). OpenEval finds use of published data for classification appropriate. Peer reviewers accept background context broadly but do not specifically evaluate these localization claims.

Minimal overlap on structural model correlation (C117-C119). OpenEval finds inference reasonable though mechanism not structurally resolved. Peer reviewers do not specifically comment on structural interpretations.

Minimal overlap on wildtype ILI observations (C104-C105). OpenEval notes functional interpretation is speculative but reasonably inferred. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these background observations.
